rationale: Pulling the 40 seals out of the sea consolidation and flying them from AMS lands them on 11 Oct for about USD 3.8K, a week ahead of the induction, against USD 12K of LDs if we wait. The Antwerp reroute is USD 1.9K cheaper but lands only 2 days before need and depends on a port absorbing diverted strike volume. The 2022 Frankfurt crunch (PRE-01) showed that trucking to AMS and flying is the reliable fallback when a European gateway closes.

qa.answer: Four options. Pull the seals out of the consolidation and fly from AMS (about USD 3.8K, no slip, recommended), reroute the box via Antwerp (about USD 1.9K, lands 17 Oct if Antwerp holds), wait for the strike to end (USD 12K of LDs, Kestrel Bay moves 2 days), or induct on time and fit the seals at gearbox build (no cost if planning confirms the seals are not needed in the first 3 days).

Re-sequencing the gearbox build costs nothing, but it uses the single day of float and needs planning to confirm the seal is not on the early critical path. The cheapest freight option is Antwerp at about USD 1.9K, which leaves 2 days of margin; the recommended AMS air route costs about USD 3.8K and leaves 8.

There is no Rotterdam strike precedent, but in 2022 freighter capacity out of FRA collapsed and six nacelle and chemical shipments were stuck at the gateway (PRE-01). We trucked them to AMS and flew from there for USD 21.4K, all six landed within 2 days of plan and no induction moved.

WO-2622 inducts on Engine shop line E-17 on 19 Oct and needs 40 gearbox carbon face seals from PO line 4500018894-00010. The strike moves SHP-880509 to 22 Oct, a 3 day slip against 1 day of float, so the Kestrel Bay Cargo redelivery moves 2 days from 18 Dec to 20 Dec.
